summary: This sermon examines Revelation 12 as a 'trailer' for the Bible's unified redemptive story, showing how the woman, child, and dragon have appeared throughout Scripture from Genesis to the present. The pastor connects this cosmic narrative to the ordinances of baptism and communion, explaining how Christians participate in God's story through initial faith and ongoing faithfulness despite the enemy's continued attacks.
key_points: Revelation 12 functions as a summary of God's story from Genesis through Revelation with three main characters
Satan has been decisively defeated and thrown down but causes suffering because his time is short
Baptism embodies passing through chaos waters to salvation, like Noah's ark and the Red Sea crossing
Communion sustains believers in the wilderness, reminding them to love not their lives unto death
Christians participate through faith (baptism) and faithfulness (communion) in the already-but-not-yet kingdom
big_idea: Christians live in the tension between Christ's accomplished victory and final return, participating in God's story through baptism as initial faith and communion as ongoing faithfulness while the defeated enemy causes suffering in his limited remaining time.
title: REVELATION: God's Redemptive Story
